steps.why: Each boron is surrounded by four hydrogen atoms, two terminal and two bridging, so four orbitals are needed; one s and three p orbitals give four sp³ orbitals.
common_mistakes: Answering sp² because a single BH₃ unit is planar. In the dimer B₂H₆ each boron is bonded to two terminal hydrogens and to two bridging hydrogens it shares with the other boron, so it is sp³.
Counting only the terminal hydrogens. The two bridging hydrogens are bonded to boron as well.
steps.memory_tip: Each boron has two terminal hydrogens and shares two bridging ones, so four orbitals and sp³.
steps.margin_note: Give the answer sp³ and the reason: two terminal hydrogens and two shared bridging ones.

steps.label: Boron in borazine
lines: In borazine B₃N₃H₆ each boron atom is sp²

Each boron is bonded to two nitrogens and

the bond angles are close to 120°.

lines.text: Boron is sp³ in B₂H₆ and sp² in B₃N₃H₆

steps.why: Boron in borazine has three bonded neighbours and no lone pair, so three hybrid orbitals are needed, which is sp²; three sp² orbitals lie in one plane at about 120° to each other, so the ring is flat.
common_mistakes: Giving the same hybridisation for both compounds. Boron is sp³ in diborane and sp² in borazine.
Saying the borazine ring is not planar. Three sp² orbitals lie in one plane, so the ring is flat.
steps.memory_tip: Three neighbours means sp²; four neighbours means sp³.
steps.margin_note: Write the compound name beside each answer so the two are not mixed up.

insider_note: Two one-word answers, sp³ and sp², so add the reason — how many atoms are bonded to boron in each compound — and the page is complete.
